extra_misconceptions.fact: A wheelchair is part of the user's personal space, and grabbing it unannounced can startle the rider or tip the chair.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Pushing someone's manual wheelchair up a steep ramp without asking first is a polite way to offer quick assistance.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Exaggerated mouth movements and shouting distort natural lip shapes, making speechreading much harder for the listener.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Speaking much louder and slower helps a person who is deaf read lips more accurately during face-to-face conversations.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Many wheelchair users can stand or walk short distances but rely on a chair to conserve energy, reduce pain, or prevent falls.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Every person who uses a wheelchair is completely paralyzed and unable to stand or walk even a few steps on their own.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Non-visible conditions affect daily stamina, sensory processing, or safety and need equal accommodations and understanding.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Invisible disabilities like diabetes, epilepsy, or autism require fewer accommodations because no equipment is visible.

extra_socratic_questions: What distinguishes an accommodation that keeps expectations equal from a modification that alters the goal?
Where should a Scout position themselves when speaking for several minutes with a person who uses a wheelchair?
Why is it dangerous to grab a white cane or guide dog harness to steer a blind pedestrian across an intersection?
Which conversational habit shows respect when communicating with a deaf individual who is using a sign interpreter?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Modern agencies focus on vocational training, assistive technology, and supported employment in mainstream workplaces.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Community disability agencies only provide custodial day care rather than career placement or independent living skills.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Client confidentiality laws strictly prohibit visitors from photographing or recording identifiable participants without consent.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Visitors touring a rehabilitation center may freely photograph clients working in training rooms for their Scout notebook.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Supported employment programs place individuals in competitive community jobs alongside coworkers without disabilities.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: People with intellectual or developmental disabilities can only work in sheltered workshops isolated from the public.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Printed brochures summarize goals, whereas direct conversations reveal real funding challenges and daily client successes.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Agency literature and brochures alone give a complete picture of daily operations without speaking to staff or members.

extra_socratic_questions: What privacy rules must you follow regarding client photographs and names when touring a disability support agency?
Which agency program metric demonstrates whether vocational training leads to competitive integrated community jobs?
Under what condition does a job coach fade back direct workplace support for an adult with a developmental disability?
What specific intake questions help an agency match a new member with assistive technology for school or work tasks?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Alternative rank requirements and merit badges require formal medical documentation and council advancement committee approval.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: A Scoutmaster can informally waive any Eagle-required merit badge requirement on the spot if a Scout has a disability.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Brief simulations only show initial frustration and miss the long-term adaptations, skills, and systemic barriers people face.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Wearing a blindfold or sitting in a wheelchair for ten minutes teaches you everything about living with a disability.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Scouts with disabilities earn the exact same merit badges using reasonable accommodations and adaptive equipment as needed.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Scouts with physical or sensory disabilities must earn separate special merit badges rather than standard Scouting badges.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Personal medical history is private, so interviews should focus on daily experiences, goals, interests, and accessibility.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Asking a person with a disability how they were injured should be your very first question during an introductory chat.

extra_socratic_questions: Under what condition does Scouts BSA approve an alternative advancement requirement for a Scout with a permanent disability?
Which interview questions invite a fellow Scout to share candidly about camp barriers without prying into medical history?
What happens to patrol cohesion when adaptive gear and pacing are built into a campout plan before leaving home?
Why is it dangerous to modify technical safety gear on a campsite climbing tower without certified adaptive hardware?

extra_misconceptions.fact: An overly steep ramp is a tipping hazard; standard accessibility requires a maximum 1:12 slope and level landing pads.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Any ramp added over a set of front steps makes a building accessible, regardless of how steep or narrow the ramp is.

extra_misconceptions.fact: True restroom accessibility requires knee clearance under the sink, insulated pipes, and fixtures within seated reach range.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: A wide restroom stall is fully accessible even if the paper towel dispenser and sink controls are mounted high on the wall.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Comprehensive site audits also inspect Braille signage, tactile warning domes, acoustic clarity, and visual fire alarms.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Accessibility audits only need to measure physical wheelchair clearances at doorways, parking lots, and elevators.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Blocking the striped access aisle prevents side-entry wheelchair vans from deploying their ramps and traps the driver.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: The striped access aisle painted next to a van-accessible parking space can be used for temporary bike or cart storage.

extra_socratic_questions: What measurement confirms whether an entrance ramp slope and doorway clear width meet standard wheelchair access rules?
Which physical indicator at a crosswalk alerts a pedestrian using a white cane that the sidewalk ends at the street?
Where should an accessible parking space access aisle connect so a van lift user never has to roll behind parked cars?
What happens to a building's emergency evacuation safety when visual fire strobes are omitted from public restrooms?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Real advocacy amplifies the voices of people with disabilities and supports self-advocacy under the principle 'nothing about us without us.'
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Effective disability advocacy means making decisions on behalf of people with disabilities without asking for their input.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Young youth quickly grasp respectful habits when shown simple examples that put the person before the condition or tool.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Using person-first language during a Cub Scout talk is too advanced for elementary-age youth to understand or practice.

extra_misconceptions.fact: District-wide awareness programs educate general education peers, reduce bullying, and build inclusive school cultures.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: School disability awareness programs only benefit students who are enrolled in full-time special education classrooms.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Requirement 5a explicitly requires counselor approval beforehand to verify accurate terminology and respectful activities.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: A disability awareness presentation is ready to deliver to a pack before the merit badge counselor reviews the script.

extra_socratic_questions: What distinguishes self-advocacy led by people with disabilities from speaking over them during a community campaign?
Which presentation techniques keep Cub Scouts engaged with person-first language without turning disabilities into games?
Why is it important to gain your merit badge counselor's approval of your outline before presenting to a Cub Scout pack?
Where should a student look within their school district to verify how peer inclusion and anti-bullying programs work?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Patronizing praise for ordinary tasks is demeaning; genuine respect means holding age-appropriate expectations and equality.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Showing a positive attitude toward people with disabilities means treating them like fragile children who need constant praise.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Encouraging positive attitudes among others requires actively speaking up and modeling respectful language in your group.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Staying silent when peers tell jokes that mock disabilities is enough to fulfill a personal commitment to inclusion.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Inclusion commitments apply every day in troop meetings, school hallways, sports teams, and neighborhood conversations.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: A personal inclusion commitment only applies when volunteering at a special event or disability service organization.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Pity creates social distance, whereas disability awareness builds empathy, equal partnership, and barrier-free teamwork.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Feeling sympathy or pity for a classmate with a disability is the primary goal of completing this merit badge requirement.

extra_socratic_questions: What specific patrol leadership actions turn a vague promise to be friendly into measurable inclusion at troop meetings?
Which response strategy works best when you hear a peer use a disability label as an insult during a campout or game?
What happens to a new Scout's sense of belonging when troop games are chosen so every member can participate fully?
Where can you record and track your personal inclusion commitments so you can evaluate your follow-through over time?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Physical therapists focus on gross motor strength and mobility, while occupational therapists focus on daily living skills.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Physical therapists and occupational therapists perform the exact same job duties and can be used interchangeably.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Special educators, audiologists, prosthetists, recreational therapists, and vocational counselors also provide vital services.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Only medical doctors and nurses have professional careers that provide direct services to people with disabilities.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Speech-language pathologists require a master's degree and clinical fellowship, while audiologists need a doctoral degree.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: An undergraduate bachelor's degree alone qualifies someone to practice independently as a licensed audiologist or SLP.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Certified orientation and mobility specialists complete rigorous university coursework and blindfolded clinical internships.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Orientation and mobility specialists simply issue white canes without needing specialized graduate training or certification.

extra_socratic_questions: What distinguishes the clinical goals of an occupational therapist from those of a physical therapist in rehabilitation?
Which supervised clinical fieldwork and board exams are required before an assistive technology or therapy specialist practices?
Under what condition does a speech-language pathologist prescribe an augmentative communication device for a client?
What continuing education requirements keep a licensed special education teacher or rehabilitation counselor current?
